page: Amazon Web Services r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at speeds up to 3.7 GHz. The compute layer includes instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The server is configured with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark measurements indicate robust performance across multithreaded compute, memory, and database metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 62,261.4 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 19,786.0, alongside strong throughput in Clang software compilation (45,541.0) and ray tracing (57,822.0). In-memory database workloads demonstrate elevated throughput, logging 78.07 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and a strong PassMark database operations score of 27,191.93. Large block uncached memory writes hit 105.97 GB/sec, while small block cached reads peak at 4,741.49 GB/sec. For small-scale language model inference, it processes prompts at 4,611.49 tokens per second on a 135M model.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of dedicated local NVMe storage and zero integrated hardware GPUs. Workloads requiring persistent storage must rely on external network-attached volumes over its baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. While single-core synthetic stress testing falls within the median range, the combination of 32 dedicated AMD cores and substantial DDR5 bandwidth delivers efficient density for large datasets.

The r7a.8xlarge is structured for memory-intensive production tasks, including in-memory databases like Redis, large enterprise relational database engines, distributed caching nodes, memory-heavy ETL pipelines, and mid-tier CPU-based AI inference workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by the AWS Nitro System and AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processors. It is equipped with 32 dedicated cores running at 3.7 GHz, delivering strong multithreaded compute validated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 19,786.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 62,261.4. The instance provides 256.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, matching an 8:1 GB-per-core ratio, while omitting bundled local storage and GPUs. In-memory data structures perform exceptionally well, achieving 78.07 million Redis SET operations per second and 4,741.49 GB/sec in small cached reads. Networking sits at a 12 Gbps baseline. Lacking local NVMe disks, it relies on network storage, making it best fitted for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching systems, large-scale ETL pipelines, and specialized CPU-driven inference tasks.
